precepts.text: When the Philistines spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim, David enquired of the Lord. David used to talk to the Lord before he made decisions, and we have to learn to do that: Lord, should I do this? If it is not right, shut it down. The Lord said, Thou shalt not go up; but fetch a compass behind them, and come upon them over against the mulberry trees. And when thou hearest the sound of a going in the tops of the mulberry trees, then thou shalt bestir thyself: for then shall the Lord go out before thee, to smite the host of the Philistines. The Lord goes out before you, fighting with you. And when you read the Maccabees, angels came down and fought with Judas Maccabeus too.
precepts.point: This day will the Lord deliver thee into mine hand; that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel. And all this assembly shall know that the Lord saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is the Lord's.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
“And the Philistines came up yet again, and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim.” “And when David enquired of the Lord”: David sought counsel of the Lord. David used to talk to the Lord: Lord, should I go up now? Should I do this? Should I do that?

We have to learn to do that. Before you make a decision, talk to the Lord: I want to do this, but show me what's right, show me should I do this or not; and if it's not right, Lord, shut it down. Sisters, do that when you are marrying some of these brothers: Lord, if this brother ain't right, shut it down. Brothers, do that too: Lord, if this sister is a demon, make me see it. You can talk to the Lord. He does hear you; you are not talking to yourself.

The Lord answered, “Thou shalt not go up; but fetch a compass behind them, and come upon them over against the mulberry trees.” Don't go up right now; go around them and come up behind them, behind the mulberry trees. This goes back to the Lord teaching David how to war.

“And let it be, when thou hearest the sound of a going in the tops of the mulberry trees, that then thou shalt bestir thyself: for then shall the Lord go out before thee, to smite the host of the Philistines.” See in your mind what is taking place: when you hear me running on top of the mulberry trees, the Lord running on top of the trees, then rush yourself. I am going out before you. I'm there fighting with you, David, and we are going to smite the host of the Philistines.

That is the wars of the Lord, and it is what David meant before Goliath: “for the battle is the Lord’s, and he will give you into our hands.” The Lord goes out before his people and fights with them. When you read the Maccabees, angels came down and fought with Judas Maccabeus too, shielding him so nobody could hit him.

precepts.text: David smote the Jebusites and dwelt in the fort, the city of David.
precepts.point: He that remaineth shall be for our God, a governor in Judah, and Ekron as a Jebusite: as David smote the Jebusites and Solomon levied a tribute of bondservice on those left in the land, they will be our servants. No oppressor shall pass through them any more, for now have I seen with mine eyes, as God looked upon the children of Israel and had respect unto them.

note.label: Zionism in the Face of Syria & Hezbollah

precepts.why:
Zechariah 9:7 ends: “but he that remaineth, even he, shall be for our God, and he shall be as a governor in Judah, and Ekron as a Jebusite.” He that remaineth is you and I. And on the map, Ekron sits right there above Jerusalem.

What does it mean to be as a Jebusite? “And David said on that day, Whosoever getteth up to the gutter, and smiteth the Jebusites, and the lame and the blind, that are hated of David’s soul, he shall be chief and captain. Wherefore they said, The blind and the lame shall not come into the house. So David dwelt in the fort, and called it the city of David.”

When you read the history, David smote the Jebusites and made them servants. That is what he did. So when Zechariah says “Ekron as a Jebusite”, the land that the Philistines hold will be brought under Israel the way David brought the Jebusites under him.

precepts.text: Samuel anointed David in the midst of his brethren.
precepts.point: Even before the split, the men of Israel quarrelled with Judah over the king, saying, we have ten parts in the king. The words of Judah were fiercer, and the enmity stayed.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

precepts.why:
David was anointed more than once, and it starts here in Bethlehem: “Then Samuel took the horn of oil, and anointed him in the midst of his brethren: and the Spirit of the Lord came upon David from that day forward.” Samuel anointed him in the midst of his brethren, and the Spirit of the Lord stayed on him from that day.

After Saul was dead, David went up to the cities of Hebron, and the men of Judah came and anointed David king over the house of Judah. So he was anointed again in Hebron, but only over Judah; he was the king of Judah in Hebron.

Then all the tribes came: “Then came all the tribes of Israel to David unto Hebron, and spake, saying, Behold, we are thy bone and thy flesh.” They remembered that “when Saul was king over us, thou wast he that leddest out and broughtest in Israel”, and that the Lord had said, “Thou shalt feed my people Israel, and thou shalt be a captain over Israel.” So “they anointed David king over Israel.” Now he is king over all twelve. “In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months: and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty and three years over all Israel and Judah”: both kingdoms. And “David took the strong hold of Zion: the same is the city of David.” Zion is the city of David.

But the beef was already there before the split. In 2 Samuel 19 the men of Israel asked, “Why have our brethren the men of Judah stolen thee away”; Judah answered, “Because the king is near of kin to us”: he is our tribe. Israel said, “We have ten parts in the king, and we have also more right in David than ye”: there are more of us than you, why can't we anoint him over here? “And the words of the men of Judah were fiercer than the words of the men of Israel.” Judah cursed Ephraim out, and that enmity between the two stayed.

Ephraim felt more entitled, and in a way rightfully so: Joseph saved Israel from starvation in Egypt, Joshua of Ephraim brought us into the land and gave out the allotments, and Ephraim held Shiloh, Bethel and the first places of worship. So the anointing that began in the midst of David's brethren is also where the dividing hatred between Judah and Ephraim shows itself, a rivalry that went on long after David.

precepts.text: The Jebusites said David could not come in hither, but David took the stronghold of Zion, the same is the city of David.
precepts.point: The people that were left of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, whom Israel was not able utterly to destroy, upon those did Solomon levy a tribute of bondservice unto this day. They were forced to become our bondservants.

note.label: Joshua 15: The Lot of the Tribe of Judah

precepts.why:
The children of Judah could not drive out the Jebusites, and they dwelt with Judah at Jerusalem unto this day. Later on David conquered this place. “And the king and his men went to Jerusalem unto the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land: which spake unto David, saying, Except thou take away the blind and the lame, thou shalt not come in hither: thinking, David cannot come in hither.” The Jebusites thought David could not come in, that he was not getting past those walls.

“Nevertheless David took the strong hold of Zion: the same is the city of David.” Whosoever got up to the gutter and smote the Jebusites would be chief and captain. “So David dwelt in the fort, and called it the city of David. And David built round about from Millo and inward.” What Judah could not do in Joshua's day, David did.

precepts.text: Not until king David went up against the Jebusites was the strong hold of Zion taken; that is when Jebus became the city of David.
precepts.point: Jerusalem is called Jebus here because the Jebusites, the original inhabitants of Jerusalem, still dwelt in it; this is before David rose up and took it from them. When Israel came out of the wilderness, the promised land was inhabited primarily by Canaanites, and the children of Judah could not drive the Jebusites out.

note.label: Judges 19: The Levite's Concubine at Gibeah

precepts.why:
This is before David rose up and took Jerusalem from the Jebusites. “And the king and his men went to Jerusalem unto the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land: which spake unto David, saying, Except thou take away the blind and the lame, thou shalt not come in hither: thinking, David cannot come in hither. Nevertheless David took the strong hold of Zion: the same is the city of David.” Not until king David went up against the Jebusites was the strong hold of Zion taken; that is when Jebus became the city of David.

In the Levite’s day it was still a city of strangers. That is why, even in those wild days, he would not lodge with heathens but passed over to lodge with his brothers in Gibeah or in Ramah.

precepts.text: Saul took David that day and would let him go no more home; he made David his armourbearer and captain of his host.
precepts.point: David was thirty years old when he began to reign, a young man, and he reigned forty years: seven years over Judah in Hebron, and thirty and three years over all Israel and Judah in Jerusalem.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

precepts.why:
When the tribes came to Hebron they said, “Also in time past, when Saul was king over us, thou wast he that leddest out and broughtest in Israel.” This is where that began: “Saul took him that day, and would let him go no more home to his father’s house.”

Saul made David his armourbearer and captain of his host. So even while Saul was king, David was the one leading Israel out to war and bringing them in, and the people remembered it when they came to make him king over all Israel.

precepts.text: David went out whithersoever Saul sent him and behaved himself wisely; Saul set him over the men of war.
precepts.point: David was thirty years old when he began to reign, a young man, and he reigned forty years: seven years over Judah in Hebron, and thirty and three years over all Israel and Judah in Jerusalem.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

precepts.why:
“And David went out whithersoever Saul sent him, and behaved himself wisely: and Saul set him over the men of war, and he was accepted in the sight of all the people.”

That is what the tribes meant when they said David was the one “that leddest out and broughtest in Israel.” Saul set him over the men of war, and David fought many wars. The Lord had already said to him, “Thou shalt feed my people Israel, and thou shalt be a captain over Israel.” He was a captain before he was a king.

So when all the elders came to Hebron and anointed him king over Israel, it was the people who had already accepted him in their sight making it official over the whole nation.

precepts.text: The women sang, Saul hath slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands; David had fame among the people while Saul was king.
precepts.point: David was thirty years old when he began to reign, a young man, and he reigned forty years: seven years over Judah in Hebron, and thirty and three years over all Israel and Judah in Jerusalem.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

precepts.why:
“And the women answered one another as they played, and said, Saul hath slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands.”

David had fame among the people while Saul was still king. That is why the tribes could say, “Behold, we are thy bone and thy flesh”: we are kinsmen, related to thee, and we know thee. They remembered the man who led them out and brought them in.

So all the elders came to the king to Hebron, and “they anointed David king over Israel.” He was thirty years old, a young man, and he reigned forty years: seven years and six months over Judah in Hebron, and thirty and three years over all Israel and Judah in Jerusalem.

precepts.text: If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men; we are at peace with all men now.
precepts.point: Our forefathers were aggressive toward the nations in that time period, but that is not the time we are in now. The word tells us to be at peace with all men; we do not break the laws of the land, for this is at present a spiritual battle and not a physical one.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

precepts.why:
David took the strong hold of Zion from the Jebusites. They thought to put a stipulation on him, “Except thou take away the blind and the lame, thou shalt not come in hither”, thinking he could not come in at all. They did not reckon with a man who had already slain his ten thousands. “Nevertheless David took the strong hold of Zion.” When the scripture says nevertheless, it means the thing will be done regardless of what stands against it.

Our forefathers were aggressive toward the nations in that time period. David was a man after God's own heart who would not let any nation stand in the way of the Lord's people, and “the Lord God of hosts was with him.”

But that is not the time we are in now. “If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.” We are at peace with all men. We do not break the laws of the land, for this is at present a spiritual battle and not a physical one.

precepts.text: The LORD is a man of war: the LORD is his name; no war did Israel win alone.
precepts.point: The Philistines left their images there, and David and his men burned them. David knew the law, that the graven images of the nations were to be burned with fire and their silver and gold not desired, lest a man be snared and cursed by bringing an abomination into his house.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

precepts.why:
“The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name.” When the Philistines came up to seek David, he did not go to war on his own strength. He enquired of the Lord, “Shall I go up to the Philistines? wilt thou deliver them into mine hand?” He knew where his power lay.

The Lord answered, “Go up: for I will doubtless deliver the Philistines into thine hand.” And when David smote them he gave the Lord the victory: “The Lord hath broken forth upon mine enemies before me, as the breach of waters.” So he called the place Baal-perazim.

The Philistines had already lost their champion Goliath, and still they came to challenge this man. But the victory was the Lord's, because the Lord is a man of war. No war did Israel win alone.

precepts.text: The graven images of their gods shall ye burn with fire; desire not the silver or gold on them, lest thou be snared.
precepts.point: The Philistines left their images there, and David and his men burned them. David knew the law, that the graven images of the nations were to be burned with fire and their silver and gold not desired, lest a man be snared and cursed by bringing an abomination into his house.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

precepts.why:
At Baal-perazim “they left their images, and David and his men burned them.” David knew the law: “The graven images of their gods shall ye burn with fire: thou shalt not desire the silver or gold that is on them, nor take it unto thee, lest thou be snared therein: for it is an abomination to the Lord thy God.”

He did not keep the Philistines' gods as spoil or desire the silver and gold on them. He burned them, exactly as the law commanded, lest a man be snared by them.

precepts.text: Bring not an abomination into thine house; utterly detest and abhor it, for it is a cursed thing.
precepts.point: The Philistines left their images there, and David and his men burned them. David knew the law, that the graven images of the nations were to be burned with fire and their silver and gold not desired, lest a man be snared and cursed by bringing an abomination into his house.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

precepts.why:
The law goes on: “Neither shalt thou bring an abomination into thine house, lest thou be a cursed thing like it: but thou shalt utterly detest it, and thou shalt utterly abhor it; for it is a cursed thing.”

That is why David and his men burned the images the Philistines left behind. To carry them home would have brought an abomination into the house and made a man a cursed thing like it. David knew the law and kept it, even in the heat of victory.

precepts.text: I will give peace in the land, and ye shall lie down, and none shall make you afraid.
precepts.point: Because David meditated in the law, he knew the Lord was his power source. The Lord had promised that five would chase a hundred and a hundred put ten thousand to flight, that He would cause Israel's enemies to be smitten and to flee seven ways. David leaned wholly on that promise.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

precepts.why:
“And I will give peace in the land, and ye shall lie down, and none shall make you afraid: and I will rid evil beasts out of the land, neither shall the sword go through your land.”

The Philistines came up yet again and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim. The Most High hardened the hearts of the nations, so it was of God that they came back. But David was not afraid, because he meditated in the law and knew the promise: peace in the land, and none to make Israel afraid. The Lord was his power source.

precepts.text: Five of you shall chase an hundred, and an hundred of you shall put ten thousand to flight.
precepts.point: Because David meditated in the law, he knew the Lord was his power source. The Lord had promised that five would chase a hundred and a hundred put ten thousand to flight, that He would cause Israel's enemies to be smitten and to flee seven ways. David leaned wholly on that promise.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

precepts.why:
“And five of you shall chase an hundred, and an hundred of you shall put ten thousand to flight: and your enemies shall fall before you by the sword.”

David leaned wholly on that promise. When he enquired this time, the Lord gave him war strategy: “Thou shalt not go up; but fetch a compass behind them, and come upon them over against the mulberry trees.” David sought counsel again rather than assume the last answer.

When he heard “the sound of a going in the tops of the mulberry trees”, then “shall the Lord go out before thee, to smite the host of the Philistines.” The Lord fought before him, and David smote the Philistines from Geba until he came to Gazer. That is how a few chase an hundred and an hundred put ten thousand to flight.

precepts.text: The LORD shall cause thine enemies to be smitten before thy face and to flee seven ways.
precepts.point: Because David meditated in the law, he knew the Lord was his power source. The Lord had promised that five would chase a hundred and a hundred put ten thousand to flight, that He would cause Israel's enemies to be smitten and to flee seven ways. David leaned wholly on that promise.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

precepts.why:
“The Lord shall cause thine enemies that rise up against thee to be smitten before thy face: they shall come out against thee one way, and flee before thee seven ways.”

The Philistines rose up against David twice in the valley of Rephaim, and twice the Lord caused them to be smitten before him. The second time the Lord himself went out before David, and the host was smitten from Geba to Gazer. David knew this promise from the law, and because he knew it, he knew the Lord was his power source.

precepts.text: All the people of the earth shall see that thou art called by the name of the LORD, and be afraid of thee.
precepts.point: Because David meditated in the law, he knew the Lord was his power source. The Lord had promised that five would chase a hundred and a hundred put ten thousand to flight, that He would cause Israel's enemies to be smitten and to flee seven ways. David leaned wholly on that promise.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

precepts.why:
“And all people of the earth shall see that thou art called by the name of the Lord; and they shall be afraid of thee.”

That was the blessing on Israel when they obeyed, and it was on David. He did “as the Lord had commanded him”, and the Lord went out before him. The nations that came against him saw a people called by the name of the Lord, and they were smitten and afraid.

precepts.text: By thee I have run through a troop, and by my God have I leaped over a wall; David knew his power source.
precepts.point: Because David meditated in the law, he knew the Lord was his power source. The Lord had promised that five would chase a hundred and a hundred put ten thousand to flight, that He would cause Israel's enemies to be smitten and to flee seven ways. David leaned wholly on that promise.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

precepts.why:
David said it himself: “For by thee I have run through a troop; and by my God have I leaped over a wall.”

David knew his power source. That is why he enquired of the Lord before going up against the Philistines, and why he waited for the sound of a going in the tops of the mulberry trees before he moved. It was by his God that he ran through the host of the Philistines, not by his own strength.

precepts.text: He teacheth my hands to war, so that a bow of steel is broken by mine arms; David's strength was of the Most High.
precepts.point: Because David meditated in the law, he knew the Lord was his power source. The Lord had promised that five would chase a hundred and a hundred put ten thousand to flight, that He would cause Israel's enemies to be smitten and to flee seven ways. David leaned wholly on that promise.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

precepts.why:
“He teacheth my hands to war, so that a bow of steel is broken by mine arms.”

David's strength was of the Most High. The Lord taught him war in the plainest way at the mulberry trees: go not up, fetch a compass behind them, and move when you hear the sound in the tree tops. David did so, “as the Lord had commanded him”, and smote the Philistines from Geba to Gazer. The hands were David's, but the Lord taught them to war.

precepts.text: As the Most High broke forth upon the Philistines at Baal-perazim, so shall He do this strange act.
precepts.point: The Most High shall rise up as in mount Perazim and be wroth as in the valley of Gibeon to do His strange work; therefore be not mockers, for a consumption is determined upon the whole earth.

note.label: Isaiah 28: Woe to the Drunkards of Ephraim and Precept Upon Precept

precepts.why:
“For the Lord shall rise up as in mount Perazim, he shall be wroth as in the valley of Gibeon, that he may do his work, his strange work; and bring to pass his act, his strange act.” Mount Perazim is where David fought the Philistines: “And David came to Baal–perazim, and David smote them there, and said, The Lord hath broken forth upon mine enemies before me, as the breach of waters. Therefore he called the name of that place Baal–perazim.”

As the Most High broke forth upon the Philistines at Baal-perazim, like the breach of waters, so shall he do this strange act. When the overflowing scourge passes through, the leaders shall be trodden down by it; “the bed is shorter than that a man can stretch himself on it: and the covering narrower than that he can wrap himself in it”, so their lies will not be their refuge when judgment comes. “Now therefore be ye not mockers, lest your bands be made strong”, for a consumption is “determined upon the whole earth.”
